activity_title: Implemented all six Priority-2 calculation fixes and passed 42/42 automated checks
activity_summary: Fixed the six incorrect calculations identified in the read-only validation phase: (1) Leakage GBP for Others was hardcoded 0.00, now signed Invoice minus Forecast = -87.55; (2) KPI 22 daily reconciliation no longer reports a false 100% PASS, now NOT COMPUTABLE; (3) KPI 26 average dispute age resolved to NOT COMPUTABLE with Days Open and Date Raised blanked consistently in the Leakage Register; (4) Variance % now applies the workbook IFERROR(...,0) so Wayfair renders 0% not blank; (5) renamed Expected GBP to Estimated Cost (Historical Baseline) everywhere, 0 occurrences of the old label remain; (6) refreshed the snapshot to as-of 2026-07-09. Also corrected Open Disputes from 2 to 1 because Killed is not an open status per README S13. No schema changes, no PostgreSQL writes.
reusable_pattern: Signed-variance rule: Leakage = Invoice - Forecast must stay signed; never clamp a negative variance to 0 to make a carrier look compliant
validation_rule: A KPI whose inputs are unavailable must render NOT COMPUTABLE, never a passing value; and the blank rule must be applied consistently to every field derived from the same missing input
gap_or_risk: KPI 22 previously displayed 100% PASS while its closure input (label_type) did not exist, overstating control coverage to the Accounts team
next_action: Re-point Forecast GBP to blos.postage once destination_zone and price_with_tax are populated

activity_title: Eliminated silent blanks: 23 blocked fields now render an Unavailable pill naming the exact requirement
activity_summary: Added a REQ lookup and un() helper to the dashboard so every field blocked by missing data renders an Unavailable pill with a tooltip naming the precise blocker (for example Requires order_shipping_billing_detail.label_type (schema), or Requires the rate card - blos.postage). Replaced 23 silent blanks across Daily Control, Weekly Invoice Check, Booking Log and the Leakage Register. A silent blank reads as zero or as nothing-to-see; a labelled pill reads as a known gap with an owner.
reusable_pattern: Blocked-field pill pattern: never render an empty cell for missing data - render a typed Unavailable pill whose tooltip names the exact table.column and whether the blocker is schema or ETL
validation_rule: Every blocked field must state its blocker; a blank cell is a defect, not a value
gap_or_risk: Footnotes and metadata notes do not undo a misleading column header - disclosure must sit on the surface the user reads
next_action: Rename the Invoice GBP column header to Actual Charge GBP (pending user approval)

activity_title: Traced the Invoice GBP column to its source and found it is carrier_charge mislabelled as an invoice
activity_summary: The user challenged the provenance of the Invoice GBP column in the Weekly Invoice Check. Read the render code rather than answering from memory: the column key is actual_gbp, populated by SUM(order_shipping_billing_detail.carrier_charge). Re-derived it live and it reproduces to the penny (3634 labels, 12525.72 total, DHL 3038.22). Swept every column in every schema for %invoice% and found exactly two hits, neither usable: amazon_returns.invoice_number (marketplace return reference) and supplier.invoices.invoice_date (inbound container freight, 22 rows, 0 in W27). Conclusion: no carrier invoice exists anywhere in the database. The Weekly Invoice Check therefore compares carrier_charge against an 8-week moving average of itself - it measures cost drift, not billing accuracy, and is structurally incapable of detecting carrier overbilling, which is the tab's entire purpose. The number is correct and traceable; the column name is not.
evidence_refs: information_schema sweep for %invoice% = 2 hits, both out of scope; dashboard line 765 label Invoice GBP (G) bound to key actual_gbp
reusable_pattern: Provenance trace pattern: when a figure is challenged, read the render binding and re-derive from source rather than answering from memory or from prior documentation
validation_rule: A column header is a claim about provenance; a substitute value must be renamed on the surface, not merely footnoted
gap_or_risk: CRITICAL - the Weekly Invoice Check cannot detect carrier overbilling because the carrier invoice never enters the system; the tab silently validates nothing
next_action: Create the carrier_invoice table (requirements doc S6.1) - this is the single highest-value gap

activity_title: Discovered order_transaction is line-item grain; naive joins overstate postage by GBP 1215.88
activity_summary: While re-deriving the DHL figure the total failed to reconcile. Root cause: public.order_transaction is one row per order LINE ITEM keyed on order_item_info, not one row per order. Joining it directly to order_shipping_billing_detail duplicates carrier_charge on multi-line orders. Naive join yields 4002 labels and 13741.60; deduplicating to order grain with SELECT DISTINCT order_id first yields the correct 3634 labels and 12525.72. I made this exact mistake mid-investigation and caught it only because the total did not tie out. Documented as a standing grain warning.
evidence_refs: Naive join 4002 rows / 13741.60 vs DISTINCT order_id 3634 rows / 12525.72; delta 1215.88
reusable_pattern: Grain-check pattern: before aggregating across a join, confirm the fact table's grain against its primary key; reconcile the aggregate to a known control total before publishing
validation_rule: All postage aggregates must deduplicate order_transaction to order grain before joining to shipping detail
gap_or_risk: Any downstream report joining these two tables naively will silently overstate postage cost by roughly 10%
next_action: Publish the grain warning to the data team as section 1 of the requirements document

activity_title: Quantified 173 NULL carrier_charge rows and separated legitimate zeros from genuine gaps
activity_summary: Found 173 of 3634 W27 labels (4.8%) carry carrier_charge IS NULL. SUM() skips NULLs, so carrier totals silently understate. Decomposed by carrier family: 146 are Wayfair, which is legitimate because postage is GBP 0 to us per the README, but the value should be stored as 0.00 rather than NULL; 10 Evri and 17 Others are genuine data gaps requiring investigation. The per-label average incidentally dodges the problem by dividing by 3461 non-null rows, which masks the issue rather than fixing it.
evidence_refs: W27: null_charge total 173 = Wayfair 146 + Evri 10 + Others 17; avg cost 12525.72/3461 = 3.62
reusable_pattern: NULL-vs-zero discipline: a known-zero cost must be stored as 0.00; NULL means unknown and must never be silently summed away
validation_rule: Distinguish structural zeros from missing values before aggregating; report the NULL count alongside any SUM
gap_or_risk: Carrier totals understate by an unquantified amount because 27 genuinely missing charges are summed as if absent
next_action: Populate Wayfair carrier_charge as 0.00 and investigate the 27 genuine NULLs

activity_title: Re-verified the live schema and disproved three of my own previously documented findings
activity_summary: Re-derived the schema from the live database instead of trusting documentation 13-15, and found three prior claims are now false. (1) blos.postage was documented as existing with 0 rows; it now holds 753 rows, so the rate card IS in PostgreSQL and the remaining problem is column coverage, not emptiness. (2) public.shipment does not exist at all (to_regclass returns NULL), so every ticket saying add public.shipment.label_type is unactionable - label_type belongs on order_shipping_billing_detail. (3) Rate card staleness is 189 days from blos.postage.effective_date 2026-01-01, not the 311 days computed from the workbook. Newly discovered and previously unlogged: the rate card contains ZERO DHL rows and zero GLS rows, yet DHL is 514 labels and GBP 3038.22 in W27 - the second-largest carrier by spend cannot be priced at all. Also found destination_zone is 100% NULL (753/753), price_with_tax populated on only 45 of 753 rows, and Royal Mail coexists with ROYAL MAIL as separate carrier_name values.
evidence_refs: blos.postage = 753 rows, 6 carriers, 53 services, all effective_date 2026-01-01, destination_zone 753/753 NULL, price_with_tax 45/753, dhl_rows 0; to_regclass('public.shipment') = NULL
reusable_pattern: Zero-trust re-verification: never carry a schema fact forward from a prior report - a database that was audited days ago has already changed; re-derive every absence and every count
validation_rule: Documented blockers must be re-verified against the live schema before being published as requirements, because backfills and migrations silently invalidate them
gap_or_risk: Prior documentation 13-15 contains three now-false schema claims that would have been sent to the database team as tickets
next_action: Correct documentation 13-15 or supersede them with the requirements document

activity_title: Traced sample order 203-4879249-8301944 end to end and classified it as domestic
activity_summary: Pulled every column from every table referencing the order. One line item, one shipment row, zero returns, zero messages, and notably zero rows in amz_order_expenses. Classified as local/domestic UK from warehouse_location UK to shipping_country United Kingdom, marketplace UK, Royal Mail Tracked 48 (a domestic-only service) and a DY6 postcode. Flagged that this is inferred rather than read: there is no destination_zone column, so the dashboard cannot classify Domestic/EU/RoW from source data. The row also demonstrates the shipping_template_price defect concretely - it is 0.0 while carrier_charge is 2.72. Noted that the shipping and billing block is live customer PII (name, address, phone, email) and must never be copied into data.js, the HTML, the docs or any CSV export.
evidence_refs: order_transaction 1 row; order_shipping_billing_detail 1 row; amazon_returns 0; amz_msg 0; amz_order_expenses 0; shipping_template_price 0.0 vs carrier_charge 2.72
validation_rule: Destination classification must come from a stored destination_zone column, not inferred by comparing warehouse_location to shipping_country
gap_or_risk: Customer PII sits in order_shipping_billing_detail and must not leak into the standalone HTML dashboard or any exported CSV, none of which are access-controlled

activity_title: Authored the PostgreSQL data requirements document for the database team
activity_summary: Wrote documentation/16_postgresql_data_requirements.md, a handover specification derived entirely from the live database on 2026-07-09 with nothing carried over from earlier reports. Covers: corrections to prior reports; the order-grain warning; mandatory tables (5 usable, 3 out of scope, 3 to create); required and missing columns; nine specific defects in blos.postage; the carrier_name_map requirement covering 261 distinct free-text carrier strings; missing carrier invoice, dispute and independent-label feeds; derived-field computability matrix; and an 11-item priority order. evidence_refs: documentation/16_postgresql_data_requirements.md sections 0-9; 261 distinct carrier_name values; 8 columns to add; 3 tables to create
reusable_pattern: Requirements-handover pattern: state every absence with the query that proves it, separate schema change from data population, and rank by value-per-hour so the team can start with population wins
validation_rule: A requirements document must re-verify every claimed absence against the live database on the day it is written
